materials.disposition: reject r7 as retained replacement; preserve r4 working control and r7 failed evidence
materials.intended_improvement: Real improvement: clearly angular fragments and clustered gravel-like topology replace r4's softer fine-grain surface. At128 the grainy fragment groups are materially different from smooth silt.
materials.identity_uncertainty: Fragments also resemble broken crust or a flat camouflage stencil. Lack of directional shading preserves flatness but does not independently prove embedded gravel.
materials.scale: At128 cluster texture survives; at64 individual chips mostly merge; at32 material-specific fragment topology disappears into mottling.
materials.repeat_comparison: r4 already has repeating density bands, so recurrence is inherited rather than wholly new. r7 makes the dense clusters/open sand windows more emphatic, producing more conspicuous diagonal chains at128 and64. The gain in fragment vocabulary comes with a regression in repeat salience.
materials.flatness: No obvious raised stone highlights, side faces or cast shadows. Flat angular marks preserve the albedo intent better than shaded pebbles would.
materials.next_correction: Keep flat angular chips, but reduce broad cluster-density contrast and break connected diagonal cluster chains into smaller, irregularly distributed groups. Preserve enough local chip contrast to survive128. Do not simply blur the whole image: that would erase the actual improvement. Recompare exact repeats against r4 before retention.

materials.disposition: reject r7 as retained replacement; preserve r4 working control and r7 failed evidence
materials.intended_improvement: Broad light/dark divisions are more readable than r4's faint granular rubbed patches, but this is not a secure improvement in compacted-soil identity.
materials.identity_uncertainty: At128, the connected pale boundaries read as sweeping wave crests or shallow wind-worked banks at least as readily as compacted scuffs. Neutral first observations did not establish firm compaction.
materials.scale: At64 and32, grain fades while sweeping scalloped edges persist, strengthening the unwanted directional-wave reading.
materials.repeat_comparison: r4 has subtle recurrent rubbed mottling; r7 adds much more visible aligned sweeping light edges across the3x3 field. This is a clear repeat-salience regression.
materials.flatness: No discrete rock shadows, but connected light-to-dark swathes imply shallow relief more strongly than r4.
materials.next_correction: Return to r4 as control. Introduce sparse short, irregular, predominantly nondirectional rubbed/scuffed patches and localized grit interruptions inside a mostly smooth field. Break long light boundaries and reduce broad directional contrast; compaction should arise from smooth-versus-gritty distribution rather than crests.

materials.disposition: reject r7 as retained replacement; preserve r3 working control and r7 failed evidence
materials.intended_improvement: Visible diffuse deposition-like mottles replace the almost featureless r3 surface. This is a real increase in pattern visibility, but silt identity remains uncertain.
materials.identity_uncertainty: Soft grain-free character supports fine powder or silt; the branching bright/dark patches equally support clouds or mottled plaster. At128 identity rests on generic diffuse noise rather than a distinctive sediment cue.
materials.scale: At128 and64 the cloudy pattern is clear; at32 it is mainly generic beige mottling. A versus B distinction remains chiefly edge softness/direction and palette.
materials.repeat_comparison: r3 is exceptionally quiet with only faint broad modulation. r7 introduces conspicuous repeating diagonal cloud clusters at128 and64. This is a new prominent repeat defect relative to r3.
materials.flatness: No cracks, polygon cells, standing stones or sharp shadows. Nevertheless broad bright/dark patches can imply rolling shaded softness rather than uniformly illuminated flat deposits.
materials.next_correction: Start from r3's quiet smooth field and add fewer, much subtler, asymmetric pale silt deposits with incomplete feathered boundaries. Avoid a connected bright cloud perimeter and repetitive branching clusters. Test whether the cue remains distinguishable at128 without becoming a repeat landmark; do not treat increased contrast alone as identity.

adversarial_core_aspects.objection: Clearer texture does not prove the requested material. Cantonment remains plausibly sand banks; pan remains generic cloudy noise; gravel remains plausibly crust/stencil. At32 these distinctions weaken markedly.
adversarial_core_aspects.closure: Material-specific structure must survive128 without relying only on palette, with64/32 inspected for misleading residual cues.

adversarial_core_aspects.objection: All three r7 patterns have more conspicuous broad recurrence than their predecessors; cantonment and pan are the clearest regressions. Exact opposing edges do not prevent diagonal motif chains.
adversarial_core_aspects.closure: Compare new and predecessor3x3 views at128/64/32 and eliminate newly dominant landmarks while preserving local material identity.

adversarial_core_aspects.objection: Cantonment pale wave boundaries create false low relief; pan cloud shading is ambiguous. Gravel's flat chips avoid obvious rock relief but retain crust ambiguity.
adversarial_core_aspects.closure: Remove connected light/shadow-like edge structure. Flat color and microtexture must carry identity without sided highlights or cast shadows.

adversarial_core_aspects.objection: The nine singles share subdued earth colors, but r7 gravel/cantonment/pan have much more emphatic pattern structure than the retained slope, wadi-slope and fine open-sand-C. They can attract attention as texture fields before conveying terrain class.

family_review.singles128: All nine inspected. Open-sand-A, wadi-floor and crest are broad soft tonal fields; open-sand-C has fine directional striation; slope and wadi-slope are fine granular fields. R7 gravel is the most sharply clustered, cantonment more sweeping, pan more cloudlike. Palette coherence is broadly preserved; pattern-intensity coherence is not established.
family_review.sheet_status: Completed native128 nine-family contact sheet inspected; exact256 sheet not inspected and not needed for this scoped rejection.
family_review.approval_baseline: The selected family is an unqualified diagnostic assembly, not an approved style baseline.
family_review.sheet_observation: The sheet confirms common muted earth colors but a sharp frequency/style split: gravel's angular clusters, pan's cloudy edges, and cantonment's pale sweeping edges are more strongly patterned than open-sand-C and the fine granular slope fields. The retained pilot A/floor/crest are broad soft tonal fields, so a little modulation is already part of the family; the objection is not that every patch must be uniform. The new medium-scale motifs still carry conspicuous pattern recurrence and do not establish compaction/silt identity. Family view does not reverse the individual repeat regressions.
